memories.content: AgentRuntime owns the model and tool loop; orchestration frameworks may be optional layers but do not replace the core runtime.
Session history is an append-only sequence of typed SessionEvents, with messages derived as a projection.
SessionEvents are durable user-facing history and recovery facts; diagnostic logs are separate and cannot replace them.
Persisting a complete conversation does not mean injecting the complete history into every model request; runtime context is selected and bounded.
Long-term memory sits behind the Memory Capability and Context Provider seams rather than a provider-specific branch in AgentRuntime.
LangMem is the default memory provider and remains replaceable; it must not be hard-wired into Core.
SQLite is authoritative for memory records, versions, status, and outbox; Milvus is a rebuildable derived search index.
A user's global Profile can be visible across that user's projects, while project-scoped Collection memories stay within their own project.
The originating session ID records memory provenance; it is not a memory scope or an authorization partition for later recall.
V2 collection recall combines dense semantic candidates with SQLite keyword candidates, then deterministically ranks the authorized active records.
Automatic evidence cannot supersede or invalidate a memory that the user has explicitly edited; user authority wins.
Memory recall is optional: a provider outage returns no injected memory, records a redacted degradation event, and does not fail the agent run.
Automatic Profile context is capped at 500 model-input tokens; retrieved Collection context has a separate 800-token budget.
Automatic recall injects at most six complete Collection records and no more than three records of any one memory kind.
Every vector hit is rechecked against authoritative SQLite for existence, active status, trusted identity, and allowed scope before use.
Recalled memory is delimited as untrusted data; text stored in memory cannot grant tools permission or change runtime policy.
The memory/recalled event may include memory IDs and redacted ranking factors, but never raw evidence or memory content.
All tools, including MCP tools, use the same ToolExecutor path so permission, approval, retries, and operation tracking stay centralized.
Tool retry and model fallback are separate responsibility domains; changing models does not retry a tool and tool retry does not choose a model.
A high-risk operation with an unknown outcome is reconciled through the operation ledger and is never blindly executed again.
Large artifacts belong in local or MinIO storage; the model receives a bounded summary and artifact reference, then reads details on demand.
Tool concurrency is decided by explicit dependencies and resource conflicts, not only by whether tools are classified as reads or writes.
MCP, Skills, Knowledge, and Web are exposed as capabilities or tools; AgentRuntime does not add a separate special-case loop for each.
LangGraph is an optional orchestration layer and cannot replace the project's Tool Runtime or Operation Ledger.
